prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal] An original, single-file balloon archery game. Open [game/index.html](<WORKSPACE>/game/index.html) in a browser.

[action] I chose an untimed level with 12 balloons and 10 arrows. Drag backward to draw, follow the dotted arc, and release. Arrows can pop several balloons, with a rising score bonus for each hit. The bow twang and balloon pops are synthesized in the browser.

[result] I inspected the title and draw screens and exercised the game with mouse input in Edge. I verified Web Audio started and the mute control worked. The browser was muted during testing, so I couldn’t judge the sound by ear.

```text
PASS mouse drag produced a multi-pop: {"points":600,"popped":3,"ammo":9}
PASS quiver depletion reveals the loss screen
PASS retry resets arrows, score and balloons
PASS full mouse-played clear: {"phase":"end","points":2400,"popped":12,"ammo":4,"title":"Clear skies."}
PASS no uncaught browser exceptions
```

[next] I closed the test browser. A guardrail blocked deletion of the browser profile and test captures, which may remain under `tmp/`.
